title: The T Flip-Flop and the Excitation Tables
quickIdea: The T flip-flop toggles when T is 1 and holds when T is 0, so Q+ = T XOR Q. The excitation table runs the characteristic table backwards: given the present and next state, it says what input each flip-flop needs.
remember: T flip-flop: Q+ = T XOR Q. T = 0 holds, T = 1 toggles.
Excitation table, D: D = Q+ for both rows. Nothing to remember.
Excitation table, T: T = Q XOR Q+. A change of state means T = 1; no change means T = 0.

Excitation table, JK: 0 to 0 needs J = 0, K = X; 0 to 1 needs J = 1, K = X; 1 to 0 needs J = X, K = 1; 1 to 1 needs J = X, K = 0. Read it as: set only to go up, reset only to go down, and X elsewhere.
Excitation table, SR: 0 to 0 needs 0X; 0 to 1 needs 10; 1 to 0 needs 01; 1 to 1 needs X0. The 1-to-1 row is the one that is not the mirror of the 0-to-0 row, because S = R = 1 is forbidden.
The design flow is always the same: present state and next state give the flip-flop inputs column by column, then minimise each input over the present-state variables.

example.prompt: A two-bit saturating up-counter has the next-state table 00 to 01, 01 to 10, 10 to 11, 11 to 11. It is built from T flip-flops. What are T1 and T0?
example.work: Take T = Q XOR Q+ per bit. For Q1 the next value differs only in the row 01, so T1 = Q1'Q0. For Q0 the next value differs in every row except 11, so T0 = Q1'Q0' + Q1'Q0 + Q1Q0' = Q1' + Q0'.
example.answer: T1 = Q1'Q0 and T0 = Q1' + Q0'. This is GATE CSE 2017 Set 2 Q.42, accepted answer option (B).

gateAngle: Excitation is the bridge between a state table and gates, so it is the step most GATE counter-design questions stop at. Two shapes recur: give the table and ask for the input expressions, or give the expressions and ask for the sequence.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why does the JK excitation table contain X entries where the D and T tables contain numbers?
variations.answer: Because J and K are two inputs describing one transition. When the state must go from 0 to 1 only J matters and K may be anything; when it must stay at 1 only K matters and J may be anything. The free entry is a don't care, and it is what makes a JK design smaller than a D design.
variations.why: A don't care in the excitation table becomes a don't care in the K-map, which is where the saved gates come from.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: A three-bit counter must visit 000, 011, 101, 110 and repeat. How many T flip-flops are needed and what is T2 in the first row?
variations.answer: Three flip-flops, since there are four states and two would give only four patterns but the sequence uses specific three-bit codes. In the row 000 to 011 the high bit does not change, so T2 = 0.
variations.why: The flip-flop count comes from the number of states, ceil(log2 4) = 2, but a code that must be read as the count forces three bits. GATE separates these two ideas deliberately.

trap.what: Filling the excitation table from the characteristic table without reversing the roles of the columns.
trap.why: The characteristic table answers 'given the input, what is the next state'. The excitation table answers 'given the two states, what input do I need'. Same four rows, opposite direction, and the answers differ.
trap.counterexample: For a T flip-flop going from 1 to 1 the excitation entry is 0, while the characteristic table entry for T = 0 and Q = 1 is also 1 to 1; but for T = 1 and Q = 1 the characteristic table also says 1 to 0, which the excitation table assigns to the row 0 to 1. Confusing the two produces an inverted design.

check.question: A D flip-flop must go from 0 to 0. What is its excitation input, and what would a JK flip-flop need for the same transition?
check.answer: D = 0. JK needs J = 0 and K = X.
check.explanation: D = Q+ = 0 directly. For JK, a 0 that stays 0 must not be set, so J = 0, and resetting is irrelevant because it is already 0, so K is a don't care.

sources.title: Lecture 7 - Synchronous Sequential Logic
sources.channel: IIT Bombay, CS 226 Digital Logic Design (Ashutosh Trivedi)
sources.note: The complete slide text was served and read: the sequential definition, the synchronous and asynchronous classification, the NOR and NAND SR latch tables, the gated SR latch, the D latch, the problem with latches, the edge-triggered D flip-flop and setup and hold, the JK and T flip-flops with their characteristic equations, the analysis example, the seven-step synthesis procedure, state reduction and the binary, Gray and one-hot assignment table.

sources.title: फ्लिप-फ्लॉप (Flip-flop)
sources.note: The article was read in full and translated into English here. It gives the two stable output states, the latch name, the four kinds (SR, D, T, JK), the T characteristic equation Q_next = T XOR Q, and the combined characteristic and excitation table for D, T, SR and JK. The excitation table is the one place where a Hindi source supplied a table this repository publishes, and the table is recomputed in scripts/validate.py rather than trusted.
